title: Adjectives, comparison and number
prior_teaching_boundary: Only actual reviewed Unit1–2 form, sense and construction milestones count. Personal genitive recognition, supplied encounters and reference-only reconstruction establish no broader production milestone.
productive_outcomes: Use the complete strong/weak adjective NGDA systems and selected stem changes in ordinary attributive and predicate agreement.
Use six agreeing possessives, distinguishing possessor reference from the gender, number and case of the possessed noun.
Form and use six comparison series, selected adverb degrees, and bounded copular comparisons with a nominative standard after ðonne.
Use one through twelve in their stated count-noun frames, first through seventh as ordinals, and this/that demonstratives.
Complete Cook I.4.1–17 and original graded tasks, read the controlled account independently, and interpret the complete fourth-day source with its explicit local support.
recognition_outcomes: Identify displayed distinct instrumental forms without productive instrumental syntax.
Recognize plural ān morphology without a plural-count-one meaning.
Recognize the strong-only eall reference paradigm without productive quantifier syntax.
bounded_scope: Instrumental cells and plural ān are recognition/reference; they do not establish instrumental syntax or cardinal-one plural meaning.
Ordinary adjectives after possessives admit strong and sometimes weak; no universal possessive→weak rule.
Complete forms do not imply substantival, partitive, adverbial, participial, temporal or clause syntax beyond explicit features.
No general prefix rule, subjunctive/imperative production, perfect/passive production, or expanded comparative clause syntax.
eall strong-only reference cells/sense are new recognition; no independent production or general quantifier syntax.
Source-only connective sōðlice remains supplied despite the newly productive adverb truly sharing its invariant spelling.
All unselected variants are valid source alternatives, with no automatic extra milestones.
Audit cell recommendations are inputs to the learning contract, not assignments or milestones. Existing supplied histories remain intact.
NGDA forms and ordinary agreement are productive only where contract assigns them. Instrumental cells remain recognition reference; means/manner/measure syntax is not taught.
Agreeing possessive lemmas are separate from personal genitives. Invariant his/hiere/hiera remain the Unit2 system. sīn/self/relative uses are deferred.
eall is a new-recognition morphology reference exception, with no production or independent all-quantifier syntax. ān plural is morphological recognition only; alone is not assigned.
Other Cook comparison families, defective spatial/time degrees, higher numerals/fractions, inflected substantive4–19, and advanced comparison standards are outside this bounded unit.

Connected source-reading subjunctives, strong preterites, perfect/resultative/purpose constructions and lexical prefixed verbs require the source editor’s explicit support; adjective tables do not teach them.

audited_inflection_rules.statement: Attributive and ordinary predicative adjectives agree in gender, number and case with their noun/referent; predicate positive adjectives are strong.
Ordinary adjective after demonstrative/article is weak; comparative always weak; ordinal weak except ōðer; superlative normally weak attributively and strong in the taught predicate use.

The six selected possessives decline strongly and agree with the possessed noun, not the owner. A following ordinary adjective may be strong or weak: Cook says sometimes weak; avoid imposing one universal choice.
Bounded A + copula + comparative + ðonne + B: when A and B are the contrasted subjects, B is nominative and the repeated copula may remain unexpressed. This does not cover every comparative clause.

Distinct strong adjective/demonstrative M/N singular instrumental forms are reference recognition only; agreement, manner, means, comparison-measure and prepositional instrumental syntax are not assigned. Weak instrumental shares dative forms, not an additional taught construction.

One modifies singular count nouns; two/three inflect for plural noun gender/case. Four through twelve are taught in ordinary uninflected pre-nominal use with plural count nouns and plural verb agreement. Plural ān is reference-only, weak āna alone unassigned.
Selected adjective bases yield -e or -lice adverbs; regular degree -or/-ost, with wel/bęt/bętst memorized separately. Adverbs are indeclinable and can qualify verbs/adjectives/other adverbs.

Use the selected lemma rows, not a universal instruction to delete medial vowels. Long disyllables often shorten before vowel endings but retain the medial vowel before consonantal -ne/-re/-ra; analogical and endingless-u alternatives are lexical/pattern choices.

obligations: Display complete gōd strong and weak NGDA tables, singular/plural and all genders; show distinct strong M/N instrumental singular as recognition.
Display complete glæd short-stem contrast or a full parallel ending/stem map; explicitly mark every æ/a cell.
For micel, lȳtel, īdel, ǣmtig, yfel and ōðer, show exact diagnostic stems/endings and selected zero/u cells so every full cell is recoverable; generic syncopate is insufficient.
Give complete recoverable æppelbǣre -e, gearu u/w and hēah h-loss patterns together with their exceptions.
Other regular positives use a precise gōd/glæd pattern reference plus verified stem and sense; no redundant full table is required for each.
eall has a complete strong-only recognition/reference pattern; no independent use is assessed and no productive quantifier construction is assigned.

Make all six full strong possessive systems recoverable: mīn/ðīn, uncer/incer, ūre and ēower each need explicit stems, selected syncope, consonant-endings, N/A singular/plural diagnostics and reference instrumentals.
Explain possessor reference separately from possessed-noun agreement and contrast invariant his/hiere/hiera; personal genitive citations are separate.
Give the six exact comparison series and full representative weak comparative; explicitly list each nontransparent comparative Gpl and selected accepted variants.
Give complete recoverable strong/weak superlative patterns by the already displayed endings and exact lexical stems, with ordinary use limits.
Teach bounded copular ðonne comparison and selected adverbs, including all eight adverb surface forms, exact glosses, invariance and degree.
Adjective bases wīd/swīð/sōð are supplied citations only.
Display complete ān singular, twēgen and ðrīe gender/case systems; plural ān is explicitly recognition/reference, without a productive plural-one sense.
Give all cardinals 4–12 in ordinary invariant pre-nominal counting use and ordinals first–seventh with complete weak pattern and exceptional full ōðer diagnostics.
Display complete se/ðes demonstrative NGDA systems; prior se morphology is not new teaching, but pointing that/those is a new sense. Distinct instrumentals are reference only.
Include every assigned productive lemma/sense and diagnostic form, complete ðing and counted-lēoht scope.
Present the controlled account and all ten ungraded examples with exact approved text.
Present the complete 109-word source with every local form and construction support, preserving all source letters/length marks and ambiguity of ofer eorðan.
Preserve the seventeen exact Cook prompts and add every graded task with its key counterpart. Include the source notes and declared normalizations.

independent_source_translation.origin: New editorial source-audit translation made from the actual Old English; not learner prose or a task key.
independent_source_translation.text: God then said, “Let there now be lights in the firmament of heaven, and let them separate day and night, and let them be for signs, for seasons, for days, and for years. And let them shine in the firmament of heaven and illuminate the earth”; it then came to pass thus. And God made two great lights: the greater light for the illumination of the day, and the lesser light for the illumination of the night; and he made stars. And he set them in heaven, so that they might shine over the earth, rule over the day and the night, and separate light and darkness; God then saw that it was good. And evening and morning came to pass, the fourth day.
notes: sōðlice is a narrative connective here (source note15: Latin autem), not a compulsory emphatic claim “truly”. The English opening absorbs this connective.
“Let there be” renders a finite plural wish, not an infinitive. Each coordinated optative belongs to the wish or later purpose construction.
“Be for signs/seasons...” can idiomatically become “serve as signs...” but that is an English paraphrase, not an extra Old English verb.
The paired greater and lesser lights are unnamed in this source span. Do not replace them in the transcript or translation with sun and moon.
The closing source order and resultative formula are kept distinct from the simpler independent copula system. An idiomatic “there came evening and morning, the fourth day” preserves the sequence.
The final clauses say that the lights rule over day/night and divide light/darkness. They do not merely restate illumination.

new_material_examples.text: Gōd męte is on ðǣre eorðan.
new_material_examples.meaning: Good food is on the earth.
new_material_examples.purpose: Strong bare attributive adjective; prior locative phrase.

new_material_examples.text: Se gōda mann hæfð gōdne męte.
new_material_examples.meaning: The good man has good food.
new_material_examples.purpose: Weak determined subject versus strong bare accusative object adjective.
Weak attributive and strong predicate adjectives agree with one neuter noun.
Singular addressee; agreeing possessive chosen by possessor and inflected for the possessed object.
First-person plural possessor with masculine accusative plural agreement.
Near demonstrative and weak adjective with a neuter accusative object.

new_material_examples.text: Se mann is ieldra ðonne se fugol.
new_material_examples.meaning: The man is older than the bird.
new_material_examples.purpose: Umlaut comparative weak predicate with a parallel nominative standard.
Adverb modifying a previously taught weak action.
Dual personal subject with plural verb, distinct from cardinal plus ordinary plural noun.

new_material_examples.text: Ūre mann is on ðǣm ōðrum hofe.
new_material_examples.meaning: Our man is in the second dwelling.
new_material_examples.purpose: Agreeing possessive and exceptional strong ordinal after the article, within prior locative syntax.

new_compositions.title: Two dwellings and three birds
new_compositions.orientation: The old man is one of the builders. In his closing speech, ‘our’ includes all the builders.
new_compositions.text: Ðā gōdan męnn geworhton twā hofu. Ān hof wæs micel, and ān hof wæs lȳtel. Ðæt micle hof wæs māre ðonne ðæt lȳtle hof. Hīe sealdon ðæt micle hof ðǣm ealdan męnn. Hē hæfde ðrīe fuglas. Hē sealde his fuglum sǣd and wæter. Ðā fuglas lifdon on ðǣm miclan hofe. Se mann sægde: “Mīne fuglas sindon gōde. Ūre weorc is gōd.”
new_compositions.purpose: Connected nominal description and comparison with productive weak past verbs, ownership, counting, transfer, location and a present direct quotation. No new finite-verb system or subordinate-clause syntax.

grammar_inventory.description: Adjectives agree with their own noun/referent in case, number and gender; attributive and ordinary positive predicate uses are taught.
Complete selected strong N/G/D/A singular/plural in all genders; lexical alternations and distinct reference instrumentals are identified.
Complete selected weak N/G/D/A singular/plural; ordinary genitive plural -ra and explicitly audited comparative exceptions.
Long adjective stems: zero feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural in selected monosyllabic strong paradigms.
Short adjective stems: selected -u in feminine nominative singular and neuter N/A plural; complete lexical paradigms determine spelling.
glæd alternates æ/a in its checked cells; this is not an unrestricted substitution rule.
Selected disyllabic stems and vowel loss are taught together with exceptions; preserve the audited cell rather than delete every medial vowel.
Complete -e adjective pattern represented by æppelbǣre, distinguishing lexical -e from case endings.
Complete gearu pattern with checked u/w alternation.
Complete hēah pattern, including h loss and the selected contraction before endings.

Ordinary attributive adjectives are weak after article/demonstrative; bare ordinary adjectives are strong. After possessives Cook permits strong and sometimes weak; no universal possessive→weak rule and no new rule for adjectives after limiting genitives.
Ordinary positive predicative adjectives are strong and nominative, agreeing with the subject even when its noun phrase contains an article. Comparatives remain weak.
Recognize distinct masculine/neuter singular strong adjective and demonstrative instrumental citations; no instrumental construction is independently taught.
The six agreeing possessives have complete strong morphology. Their endings agree with the possessed noun, not the possessor; personal-genitive citations retain separate records.
Choose mīn/ðīn/uncer/incer/ūre/ēower for the possessor person/number, then inflect for the possessed head. Contrast prior invariant his/hiere/hiera. No self or sīn teaching.
Regular lēof/lēofra/lēofost series, with full assigned degree inflections.
eald/ieldra/ieldest is the assigned umlaut series; no universal umlaut instruction.
Complete selected gōd, yfel, micel and lȳtel comparison series; exact stems and superlative choices are lexical.
Comparatives are weak attributively and predicatively; full paradigms include transparently derived genitive plural contractions and licensed -ena selections.
Full strong/weak superlative morphology; ordinary attributive superlatives normally weak, taught predicate use strong. Partitive/substantival uses remain unassigned.
Bounded subject A + copula + comparative + ðonne + parallel subject B: B is nominative, with repeated copula understood. No generalized comparative-clause or genitive-standard syntax.
Selected supplied adjective citations wīd/swīð/sōð yield checked -e/-lice adverbs; no full adjective system implied by these citation bases.
Selected adverbs qualify actions or whole statements without case/number/gender agreement; sōðlice truly is distinct from the supplied source connective sense.
swīðe very qualifies an adjective; adverb has no adjective-agreement ending.
wīde/wīdor/wīdost and wel/bęt/bętst are invariant adverbial degrees; no new comparative-clause syntax.
Complete ān singular cardinal forms with singular count nouns; plural reference cells confer no productive plural-one sense.
Complete twēgen/ðrīe N/G/D/A plural across genders; no noun dual paradigm.
Checked cardinal 4–12 forms used invariantly before plural count nouns; no postposed/substantival inflection or higher-number partitive syntax.
Cardinal one with singular nouns, 2–12 with plural count nouns; numeral gender/case agrees where the selected system inflects.
Complete selected first, third–seventh weak paradigms express order. Ordinary noun case is supplied by already taught syntax; no temporal on+accusative production implied.
ōðer second remains strong even after the article; selected syncope and feminine ōðru with valid variants are explicit.
Complete ðes/ðēos/ðis system: this/these, agreeing with the noun in N/G/D/A; reference instrumentals do not create syntax milestones.
Existing se/sēo/ðæt morphology now also expresses pointing that/those; relative and general third-person pronoun uses remain unassigned.
Complete new ðing heavy-neuter paradigm in the sense thing/things; prior ordinary case constructions apply.
Counted lēoht luminary distinct from mass light; prior singular morphology retained and all four plural cases promoted to production.
Direct speech introduced by supplied cwæð, with then and connective sōðlice. Unit2 productive quotation was specifically with sęcgan.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: God cwæð ðā sōðlice = God then said; sōðlice is connective here (Latin autem).

grammar_inventory.description: Plural finite optatives express a wish/command. Bēon is not an infinitive; all coordinated verbs share the lights as subject.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: Bēon/bēon = let there be/let them be; tōdǣlen = let them separate; scīnen = let them shine; ālīehten = let them illuminate. These are actual supplied forms, with the complete wish explained.

grammar_inventory.description: on governs dative fæstnesse; ðǣre heofonan is embedded genitive feminine singular, from weak heofone.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: on ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse = in the firmament of heaven. Mark heofonan genitive and fæstnesse dative explicitly; ðǣre agrees with heofonan.

grammar_inventory.description: tō + dative expresses assigned function/purpose. Noun cells are prior; this prepositional use is not taught by Unit2 tō wyrceanne.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: tō tācnum/tīdum/dagum/gēarum = for signs/seasons/days/years; tō ... līehtinge = for the illumination of ...; genitive day/night is nested inside the dative phrase.

grammar_inventory.description: Resultative fulfillment formula; prior wæs form does not establish independent perfect/resultative syntax.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: hit wæs ðā swā geworden = it then came to pass thus / it was then so; geworden is supplied.

grammar_inventory.description: gesętte has omitted God/he subject; hīe is accusative plural object. on ðǣre heofonan has dative feminine singular heofonan, not genitive.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: And gesętte hīe = and he set them. The subject continues God/hē. on ðǣre heofonan = in heaven, with source weak-feminine dative.

grammar_inventory.description: ðæt introduces purpose; scinen, gīemden, tōdǣlden are past optatives. This is not the content-that sense.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: ðæt hīe scinen ... and gīemden ... and tōdǣlden ... = so that they might shine ... and rule over ... and separate ... . Preserve short-i scinen, unlike present scīnen at32.

grammar_inventory.description: ofer eorðan means over the earth. Source spelling eorðan is compatible with accusative or dative singular; do not require one uniquely.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: Supply the complete phrase over the earth. The task must not grade a unique case for eorðan in this phrase.

grammar_inventory.description: gīeman governs genitive in this exact construction, explicitly documented by §156f. Genitive forms themselves are prior.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: gīemden ðæs dæges and ðǣre niht = might rule over the day and the night. Here the verb governs the two genitives; this is not an of-relationship between nouns.

grammar_inventory.description: Supplied strong geseah plus content clause ðæt hit gōd wæs. New predicate-adjective morphology can be observed within supplied content-clause syntax.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs = God then saw that it was good. ðæt is a conjunction, not the article; do not require independent subordinate-clause production.

grammar_inventory.description: Closing resultative formula and source word order supplied. The new ordinal fēorða agrees with dæg; męrgen is a source vowel variant of selected morgen.
grammar_inventory.required_local_support: And wæs geworden ǣfen and męrgen se fēorða dæg = and evening and morning came to pass, the fourth day. Explain the complete formula without grading an invented unique compound-subject agreement rule.

U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.
U03-THAN.edition: R. D. Fulk, An Introductory Grammar of Old English (2014), corrected open-access reprint, June 2020.
U03-THAN.source_attribution: Beo 469 in Fulk §35. Retain Fulk’s printed betere in this evidence quotation; it is not the selected masculine comparative model in the course.
